news.h: Pantech Global to sell former expansion site in Klang for RM31.7m
news.body: Pantech Global Bhd said it is disposing of a 10-acre freehold land which it acquired less than two years ago for the expansion of its operations in Klang, for RM31.7m in cash. The planned sale comes after regulatory delays on the development of a new factory on the site, which prompted the carbon steel pipe fittings manufacturer to acquire a different parcel of land in Klang for RM29.0m in August last year under its revised development plans. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Pantech Global is selling a 10-acre freehold plot in Klang for RM31.7m in cash.
It bought the land less than two years ago to expand its operations.
The sale follows regulatory delays to a planned new factory on the site.
Those delays led Pantech to buy a different Klang parcel for RM29.0m in August last year under revised plans.
The item gives no purchase price for the plot being sold, so no gain or loss can be worked out. This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Pantech. Digest context only.

news.h: Censof gets RM10.8m contract to install financial management system
news.body: Censof Holdings Bhd has secured a contract worth RM10.8m to install a financial management system at the Malaysian Cooperative Commission. The system will be delivered under a subscription model. The scope of work covers the full system implementation process, including requirements analysis, system design, setup, configuration, customisation, testing, integration, data migration, training, commissioning and maintenance. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Censof Holdings has won a RM10.8m contract to install a financial management system at the Malaysian Cooperative Commission.
The system will be delivered on a subscription model.
The scope runs from requirements analysis and design to data migration, training, commissioning and maintenance.
The item gives no contract period, so the annual value is not known.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Censof. Digest context only.

news.h: LEAP-listed DynaFront secures discovery agreement for Indonesian insurer’s core system project
news.body: LEAP Market-listed DynaFront Holdings Bhd said its wholly-owned subsidiary, DynaFront Systems Sdn Bhd, has secured a Phase I Discovery Agreement with an established life insurance company in Indonesia to replace the insurer’s core life insurance system. The group said DynaFront Systems was selected as the appointed vendor following the customer’s evaluation process. The discovery phase is expected to take about five months from its commencement date. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: DynaFront Holdings, listed on the LEAP Market, has signed a Phase I Discovery Agreement with an unnamed Indonesian life insurer.
The project is to replace the insurer's core life insurance system.
Wholly owned DynaFront Systems Sdn Bhd was appointed vendor after the customer's evaluation.
The discovery phase should take about five months. The item gives no contract value.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of DynaFront. Digest context only.

news.h: Pahang crown prince-linked firm to buy 30.0% stake in planter Mentiga for RM21.0m
news.body: HIS TIZA Pahang Sdn Bhd, a company linked to the Pahang crown prince, has entered into a share sale agreement with state government-owned Amanah Saham Pahang Bhd (ASPA) to acquire a 30.0% stake in Mentiga Corp Bhd for RM21.0m cash. HIS TIZA said the agreement to acquire 21.0m ordinary Mentiga shares at RM1 apiece was executed on Oct 12 and will be completed in 30 market days. The transaction price is a 72.4% premium over Mentiga's market price of 58 sen, though it sits at a discount to its unaudited net assets of RM3.17 per share as of June 30. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: HIS TIZA Pahang Sdn Bhd, linked to the Pahang crown prince, is buying 30.0% of planter Mentiga Corp for RM21.0m in cash.
The seller is state government-owned Amanah Saham Pahang Bhd. The deal covers 21.0m shares at RM1 each, signed on 12 October, with completion in 30 market days.
RM1 is a 72.4% premium to Mentiga's 58 sen market price.
It is about a 68% discount to Mentiga's unaudited net assets of RM3.17 a share at 30 June (computed here).
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Mentiga. Digest context only.

news.h: Land 33 buying one-acre George Town land for RM32.0m for future development
news.body: Land 33 Bhd is acquiring a 1.05-acre parcel with a two-storey bungalow in Penang for RM32.3m in cash for future property development. The property developer, formerly known as ACME Holdings Bhd, said the property located at Cantonment Road in George Town is currently rented to preschool operator Tadika Sains Kreatif. The property will be added to the group’s existing land bank for future development, said Land 33 in a bourse filing. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Land 33, formerly ACME Holdings, is buying a 1.05-acre plot with a two-storey bungalow on Cantonment Road, George Town.
The digest headline says RM32.0m but the body says RM32.3m in cash. This summary does not resolve the difference.
On RM32.3m, the price is about RM706 per sq ft of land (computed here, using 43,560 sq ft an acre).
The property is currently rented to preschool operator Tadika Sains Kreatif and will go into the land bank for future development.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Land 33. Digest context only.

takeaways: The IMF's new chief economist, Silvana Tenreyro, says strong AI demand has boosted growth in China, India and other Asian economies.
She says that growth has outpaced overall global trade growth.

macro.h: Tengku Zafrul: Budget 2027’s 3.3% fiscal deficit target achievable
macro.body: Malaysia is capable of achieving its fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) under Budget 2027, provided the assumptions underpinning the budget hold amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, said Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. (The Malaysian Reserve)
takeaways: Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz says Budget 2027's fiscal deficit target of 3.3% of GDP is achievable.
He makes that conditional on the budget's assumptions holding.
He cites global economic and geopolitical uncertainty as the risk.
The item does not state those assumptions.
Digest context only; sourced to The Malaysian Reserve.

reports.name: CTOS Digital Berhad
reports.catalyst: Downgraded to MARKET PERFORM from OUTPERFORM, target cut 42% to RM0.48 from RM0.83, after the cybersecurity incident disclosed on 23 September took CTOS Score and CCRIS-related services offline. The outage hits c.35% of weekly group revenue. CTOS guides a c.RM12m FY26 PATAMI hit if services resume by the third week of October. Two of four independent reviews are still pending, so Kenanga assumes services stay offline until end-December 2026. That lifts the FY26 hit to c.RM22m, with a further c.RM3m drag in 1Q27. FY26F/27F core PATAMI are cut 22.6%/3.5%. Most of the target cut comes from raising WACC to 8.1% from 5.8%.
reports.quote: Downgrade to MARKET PERFORM (from OUTPERFORM) as operational, regulatory and reputational risks have escalated.
summary: What happened. On 23 September 2026 CTOS announced that an unauthorised party had accessed one environment supporting its CCRIS consumer (self-check) business. Data files containing a limited subset of processed consumer information were accessed. CTOS says the incident was contained there, and its FI & Corporates, Commercial and International environments were not affected. CTOS Score and CCRIS-related services remain unavailable until remediation is independently validated. The Registrar of Credit Reporting Agencies and other regulators have been notified, and affected individuals informed.

How much revenue is at stake. About 35% of weekly group revenue is affected: c.55% of FI & Corporates segment revenue, c.10% of Commercial and all of Consumer. International is unaffected. CTOS's base case is one month offline to the third week of October, then a 30-day gradual recovery. On that basis it estimates an FY26 revenue hit of c.RM16m (c.5% of FY26 revenue): c.RM3m in 3Q26 and c.RM13m in 4Q26. The PATAMI hit is c.RM12m (3Q26 c.RM5m, 4Q26 c.RM7m), made up of c.RM8m business impact and c.RM4m other costs. Each extra week offline adds c.RM2.5m to the revenue hit and c.RM1.3m to the PATAMI hit.

Kenanga's harsher assumption. The external scan and forensic review are done. The vulnerability assessment and penetration testing (VAPT) and the compromise assessment are targeted for October. Kenanga 'prudently' assumes services stay offline until end-December 2026, about 10 weeks beyond management's base case. That puts the FY26 PATAMI hit at c.RM22m and pushes a c.RM3m recovery drag into 1Q27. FY26F core PATAMI is cut 22.6% to RM75.3m and FY27F 3.5% to RM88.1m, against consensus of RM95.4m and RM97.4m. DPS falls to 3.6/2.5 sen from 4.1/3.0 sen; FY26F includes a 1.1 sen special. If the outage runs into FY27, each week cuts FY27F core PATAMI by c.1.5% (c.RM1.3m). Twelve weeks would cut c.RM15.6m, or 17.7%.

Valuation and rating. The DCF target falls to RM0.48 from RM0.83 as WACC rises to 8.1% from 5.8%, on a beta of 1.7 (from 1.0) for operational, regulatory, customer-attrition and reputational risk. Kenanga says the steeper 42% cut mainly reflects the higher WACC, which it will reassess once there is more certainty. It may revisit its view after the company's briefing today. At RM0.475 the target implies about 1.1% upside (computed here). Kenanga expects the stock to trade sideways until the timing of resumption and customer retention are clearer.

Why Kenanga sees a setback, not a broken franchise. The breach was confined to consumer self-check, and c.65% of revenue continues unaffected. Lenders face high switching costs because CCRIS and Score are embedded in their credit processes. Usage of unaffected products has held steady, and key FI and corporate contracts remain in force. The share price has fallen c.25% since disclosure, which Kenanga believes largely reflects the near-term hit. After services resume, CTOS will run a 12-month programme overseen by its Board Risk and Compliance Committee: independent controls testing, ISO 27001 and RMiT compliance, and an external governance inspection. Longer-term drivers are the Consumer Credit Act 2025 (effective March 2026) opening BNPL clients, new digital banks, and possible monetisation of associate stakes. The risks it names are a longer outage and customer attrition to rival bureaus, regulatory penalties, weaker credit demand, and adverse regulatory change.

reports.name: Lianson Fleet Group Berhad
reports.catalyst: MARKET PERFORM maintained; SoP target raised to RM1.59 from RM1.54. LFG completed the purchase of Ultramax bulk carrier LFG Cengal for USD23m (c.RM93.9m), which Kenanga deems a fair price against a comparable 2013-built sale at USD23.2m. The vessel goes on an 8-year charter to LFG shareholder Liannex Corp at an estimated USD17,000/day, shielding it from the bulk spot market. That fits LFG's shift from cyclical OSVs to recurring bulk earnings. FY27F earnings are raised 5% (the table shows 1.6%; see flag). FY26F is unchanged.
reports.quote: Overall, we considered this acquisition a net positive and consistent with the group’s strategy to move into a more recurring earnings base in bulk carrier and away from a more cyclical OSV business.
summary: The vessel. LFG has acquired LFG Cengal, a Japanese-built Ultramax bulk carrier delivered in May 2013 with 61,446MT deadweight, for USD23m in cash (c.RM93.9m). Kenanga deems the price fair against the recent sale of the 2013-built Ultramax 'Ultra Saka' at USD23.2m. The note describes the acquisition as completed.

The charter. The vessel goes on a long-term 8-year charter to Liannex Corp, which the note identifies as an LFG shareholder, at an estimated daily charter rate of USD17,000. At that rate, annual charter revenue would be about USD6.2m, or roughly RM25m at the note's implied rate of about RM4.08 to the dollar (computed here; the note gives no annual revenue, vessel operating cost or margin). Kenanga says the charter keeps LFG out of the volatile bulk spot market for the whole term. Stock Information lists Liannex Maritime Sdn Bhd (22.2%) and Liannex Corp S Pte (4.3%) among major shareholders. The note does not discuss related-party terms.

Forecasts. FY26F core net profit is unchanged at RM61.6m. FY27F rises to RM105.2m on LFG Cengal's contribution (5% per the text, 1.6% per the table; see flag). Consensus is RM80.2m and RM115.5m, so Kenanga sits about 23% and 9% below (computed here). Core EPS is 5.4 and 9.2 sen, PER 28.9x and 16.9x, and DPS 4.0 sen in both years.

Valuation. The SoP target rises to RM1.59 from RM1.54. Components: OSV RM634.8m (11x FY27F PER), Drilling 40% stake RM243.1m (15x), Logistics RM417.6m (15x), Cable business RM573.1m (DCF on a 30% stake, WACC 6.1%), and warrant conversion proceeds RM323.4m assuming full conversion. That totals RM2,192.0m; less net debt of RM30.2m, over 1,359.3m fully diluted shares (1,135.9m outstanding), it gives RM1.59. Drilling and cable together are RM816.2m, about 37% of gross SoP value (computed here). These are the two ventures the note says have yet to show progress. At RM1.55 the target implies about 2.6% upside (computed here).

The case and the risks. Kenanga likes LFG for recycling capital from OSV sales at favourable prices, its venture into asset-light drilling with few local competitors, and its potential as an ASEAN Power Grid beneficiary. But the drilling and cable ventures have shown no progress to date and earnings could be delayed further, hence MARKET PERFORM. The risks it names are a global recession lowering oil prices, significant delay to the APG timeline, and inability to charter in drilling rigs at favourable rates. Today's MP and RM1.54-to-RM1.59 move are consistent with this board's 28 August Results Note (MP, RM1.54).
